item.text:
**Bottom Line**
Sharif’s 2024 crisis response was mixed in form but mostly negative in practice. There are a few real restraint signals, mainly dialogue in Azad Kashmir and counterterrorism action against militants, but the more consistent pattern is coercive: election shutdowns, protest crackdowns, internet blocks, selective detentions, and restrictive public-order rules. Confidence: moderate.

**Protective / Restraint**
- [PM condemns Besham attack, says perpetrators will be brought to justice](https://pid.gov.pk/site/press_detail/24838) | Press Information Department, Pakistan | 2024-03-27  
  Claim-level summary: After the Besham attack on Chinese nationals, Sharif condemned the killing of civilians and promised swift justice. This is a restrained response to a sudden violent crisis, but it is reactive rather than evidence of a broader crisis-protection doctrine.  
  Question IDs: `3B.9`, also `3B.4`, `3B.7`

- [PM for collective efforts to eliminate menace of terrorism](https://www.radio.gov.pk/22-06-2024/pm-for-collective-efforts-to-eliminate-menace-of-terrorism) | Radio Pakistan | 2024-06-22  
  Claim-level summary: Sharif launched a national counterterrorism campaign with provincial consensus and promised resources for the armed forces. This is the strongest evidence that he responded to real domestic violence with suppression rather than encouragement.  
  Question IDs: `3B.9`, also `3B.5`, `3B.6`, `3B.7`

- [PM Shehbaz urges AJK govt, political leadership to resolve issues through dialogue](https://www.radio.gov.pk/12-05-2024/pm-shehbaz-urges-ajk-govt-political-leadership-to-resolve-issues-through-dialogue) | Radio Pakistan | 2024-05-12  
  Claim-level summary: Sharif told local leaders in Azad Kashmir to talk with the action committee and resolve the dispute peacefully. This is a direct restraint signal in a live domestic flare-up.  
  Question IDs: `3B.9`, also `2B.7`, `3B.6`, `3B.8`

**Counterevidence**
- [Election-day internet shutdown is a reckless attack on peoples' rights](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/02/pakistan-election-day-internet-shutdown-is-a-reckless-attack-on-peoples-rights/) | Amnesty International | 2024-02-08  
  Claim-level summary: Amnesty condemned the telecom and mobile internet shutdown during the election period as a rights violation. This is coercive crisis management, not restraint, and it chilled participation at a politically sensitive moment.  
  Question IDs: `3B.9`, also `3B.1`, `3B.2`, `3B.5`, `3B.6`, `3B.8`

- [Pakistan: The new Peaceful Assembly and Public Order Act threatens the right to protest](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/09/pakistan-the-new-peaceful-assembly-and-public-order-act-threatens-the-right-to-protest/) | Amnesty International | 2024-09-09  
  Claim-level summary: Amnesty said the new protest law was rushed through and would criminalize peaceful assembly instead of protecting it. That points to administrative control and deterrence of dissent, not restraint.  
  Question IDs: `3B.9`, also `3B.5`, `3B.8`

- [Pakistani police detain two parliamentarians in swoop on ex-PM Khan's party](https://theprint.in/world/pakistani-police-detain-two-parliamentarians-in-swoop-on-ex-pm-khans-party/2260202/) | Reuters / ThePrint | 2024-09-10  
  Claim-level summary: Police detained PTI parliamentarians after a rally demanding Khan’s release. This is a selective, intimidating response to political flare-up rather than a protective one.  
  Question IDs: `3B.9`, also `3B.2`, `3B.8`

- [Pakistan Government Intensifies Crackdown on Political Dissent](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/10/09/pakistan-government-intensifies-crackdown-political-dissent) | Human Rights Watch | 2024-10-09  
  Claim-level summary: HRW reported mass arrests, tear gas, roadblocks, and mobile internet cuts during PTI protests, including arrests of peaceful protesters. This is strong evidence of retaliation and collective suppression during a domestic crisis.  
  Question IDs: `3B.9`, also `3B.1`, `3B.2`, `3B.5`, `3B.8`

- [Urgent and transparent investigation needed into deadly crackdown on opposition protesters](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/11/urgent-and-transparent-investigation-needed-into-deadly-crackdown-on-opposition-protesters/) | Amnesty International | 2024-11-27  
  Claim-level summary: Amnesty said the Islamabad crackdown involved deaths, mass detentions, and a broader intolerance of peaceful assembly. That is the clearest evidence against a restrained domestic-crisis response.  
  Question IDs: `3B.9`, also `3B.1`, `3B.2`, `3B.5`, `3B.8`

- [A dangerous digital crackdown](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/12/12/dangerous-digital-crackdown) | Human Rights Watch | 2024-12-12  
  Claim-level summary: HRW said internet shutdowns and VPN restrictions had become default tools for shutting down protests and criticism. This indicates a broader climate of censorship and control, not restraint.  
  Question IDs: `3B.9`, also `3B.5`, `3B.8`

- [End escalating attacks on minority Ahmadiyya community](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/06/end-escalating-attacks-on-minority-ahmadiyya-community/) | Amnesty International | 2024-06-21  
  Claim-level summary: Amnesty documented arbitrary arrests, police harassment, and orders blocking Ahmadi rites, with authorities failing to ensure safety. This shows that crisis-like communal tensions were not consistently met with protection and restraint.  
  Question IDs: `3B.9`, also `3B.1`, `3B.2`, `3B.7`, `3B.8`

**Search Gap**
I did not find evidence of a consistently restrained, rights-protective domestic crisis doctrine in 2024. The best positive examples are narrow and reactive, while the more reliable reporting shows a pattern of censorship, selective punishment, and force-centered response to political unrest.
